why.text: Schist terraces in mountain-sheltered valleys, with very cold winters and hot, dry summers, and many native grapes blended together.

styles.text: Reds, whites and rosados, mostly blends; also sparkling wine and fortified Moscatel do Douro.

climate.text: Very cold winters, very hot dry summers; the Marão and Montemuro mountains block wet western winds. Mean annual temperatures run 11.8 to 16.5 °C.

soil.text: Mostly schist, with patches of granite; terracing and deep ploughing reshape many soils.

tastes.text: Reds: mostly blends of native grapes, complex and rich. Whites: good aroma and complexity, often fermented or aged in wood. Rosés: pink, aromatic, soft and sweet, lightly acidic.

styles.name: Moscatel do Douro
styles.text: Fortified white made only from Moscatel Galego Branco, 16.5 to 22% alcohol.

styles.name: Espumante
styles.text: Sparkling wine with second fermentation in bottle, some vintage ones need nine months in bottle.

styles.name: Colheita tardia
styles.text: Single-harvest wine where overripe grapes can be tasted.

why.text: Mild, wet Atlantic weather favours slow ripening and fresh acidity; the mostly granite soils give the whites their mineral notes.

styles.text: White, rosé and red wines, plus sparkling and quality sparkling; late-harvest wines from overripe grapes.

climate.text: Mild, without extreme heat or cold; about 1,200 mm of rain a year, irregular, with Atlantic winds through the river valleys.

soil.text: Shallow soils, mostly granite; two narrow strips of schist cross the region.

tastes.text: Whites: pale citrine, light and fruity or floral, to mineral and honeyed. Rosés: pale pink, red fruit. Reds: ruby to dark, wild fruits. Fresh, high acidity.

styles.name: Alvarinho (Monção e Melgaço)
styles.text: Subregion wines may name Alvarinho only here; optional term «Origem do Alvarinho».

styles.name: Espumante de Vinho Verde
styles.text: Sparkling wine, white, rosé or red, made from Vinho Verde base wine.

styles.name: Palhete / Palheto
styles.text: Red wine with up to 15% white grapes; the term is mandatory.

styles.name: Vindima Tardia
styles.text: Late-harvest wine from overripe grapes; honey and dried fruit aromas, sweet.

why.text: Stony, terraced soils in the mountain-sheltered Douro valley, with very cold winters and hot dry summers, then fermentation stopped with grape spirit to keep sweetness and reach 19 to 22% alcohol.

styles.text: Fortified wine (vinho licoroso) in red, white and rosé, from Extra-Seco to Muito doce, with 19 to 22% alcohol (Branco Leve Seco from 16.5%).

climate.text: Very cold winters, very hot dry summers; the Marão and Montemuro mountains block wet western winds. Mean annual temperatures run 11.8 to 16.5 °C.

soil.text: Stony soils with no other use; steep slopes are cut into terraces.

tastes.text: Very rich, intense aroma and very long aroma and flavour, high alcohol, a wide range of sweetness and many colours.

styles.name: Vintage
styles.text: Exceptional single-harvest wine, deep in colour, full-bodied, with very fine aroma and taste.

styles.name: Tawny
styles.text: Blend aged in wood or other vessels, tawny in colour, soft, with medium persistence.

styles.name: Ruby
styles.text: Blend of young wines, fruity, red in colour, with some body.

styles.name: Colheita
styles.text: Single-harvest red or white, aged in wood at least 7 years after the harvest.

why.text: Mostly granite soils with patches of schist, and very hot, dry summers that ripen grapes fully into structured, concentrated wines.

styles.text: Reds, whites and rosados, plus sparkling wine and fortified (licoroso) wine.

climate.text: Very hot summers with high temperatures and low rainfall, giving full ripeness; the spec also stresses several microclimates.

soil.text: Mainly granite with some schist patches. Chaves: granite and clayey or gneiss-type soils. Planalto Mirandês: granite, schist and gneiss. Valpaços: granite and schist.

tastes.text: Reds: full-bodied, ruby to garnet, red fruit and vanilla, soft tannins. Whites: citrus to straw-gold, fresh tropical fruit, long finish. Sparkling: fine bubbles, fresh, fruity and light.

styles.name: Espumante Reserva
styles.text: Sparkling wine with 12 to 24 months in bottle before disgorging.

styles.name: Espumante Super-reserva
styles.text: Sparkling wine with 24 to 36 months in bottle before disgorging; also called extra-reserva.

styles.name: Espumante Velha reserva
styles.text: Sparkling wine with over 36 months in bottle before disgorging; also called grande reserva.

styles.name: Rosé
styles.text: Made by the open-run (bica aberta) method or with light skin contact.

why.text: High granite and schist slopes at 500 to 800 metres facing south, with a dry continental climate and harsh winters, give fresh, acidic whites and sparkling wines.

styles.text: Fresh whites, soft reds and rosados, and a small region that is very important for sparkling wine.

climate.text: Temperate continental and dry, with harsh winters that are very cold and wet.

soil.text: Mostly primary granite, poor in limestone, sometimes eroded and acidic schist, and low in organic matter.

altitude.text: Vineyards usually sit at 500 to 800 metres and face south.

tastes.text: Whites: soft, very fresh and fruity, with citrus aroma and natural acidity. Reds: open, fresh, lighter in body and low in acidity. Sparkling: easy to drink, ageing well.

styles.name: Espumante
styles.text: Sparkling wine, second fermentation in bottle, at least nine months' ageing from bottling.

styles.name: Reserva
styles.text: Traditional label term allowed for the appellation.

styles.name: Garrafeira
styles.text: Traditional label term allowed for the appellation.

styles.name: Colheita Seleccionada
styles.text: Traditional label term allowed for the appellation.
